newsitem.title: USA: Liposome gets expanded label for drug.
newsitem.headline: Liposome gets expanded label for drug.

text.p: Liposome Co Inc said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared for marketing an expanded indication for Abelcet to treat invasive fungal infections.
Anticipating of the expanded indication, Liposome said it has recently initiated a program to double its U.S. sales force to approximately 40 representatives, Liposome said.
The indication is for the treatment of invasive fungal infections in patients who are refractory to or intolerant of conventional amphotericin B therapy, the company said.

This represents a significant broadening in the indicated uses for the drug to include candidiasis, the most common invasive fungal infection, and cryptococcal meningitis, a relatively common infection in AIDS patients, Liposome said.
ABELCET is currently marketed in the United States for the second-line treatment of aspergillosis, a severe fungal infection.

Also, the company is conducting additional studies of ABELCET to continue to enhance the clinical data available on the product, Liposome said. Completion of the company's manufacturing plant in Indiana will permit the efficient production of ABELCET to meet demand, it said.
